claims.claim: The tutorial introduces confusing hub areas overflowing with multiple currencies, timers, and shop interfaces.

citations.review_text: It starts on ok in story mode, as it should. Then after you get done with the first portion of a mid game, you get thrown into some weird multiplayer lobby with zero explanation and no easy way to get back to the story mode you were just enjoying. Personally, I couldn't be bothered to run around some weird multiplayer lobby that I had zero interest in just to find out if there's a way back to the story line that I actually came here for. Immediate uninstall. It was barely holding my attention to begin with.

Did not like it at all, meaning that the new player experience is dogwater, terrible.
The game:
The "missions" and "fights" if you can even call them that were extremely short for the tutorial, and extremely short after the tutorial - what I think was supposed to be some kind of "story".
The combat felt good-ish, but it was over about 5 seconds before it started, every mission, every group of enemies - deleted in a second.
Even the big bad mech at the end of the tutorial - I shot it ONCE and it triggered a cutscene and exploded - I did not have a chance to even do anything, not even move.

The store(s):
When I got past the tutorial, of course I was overwhelmed by 40000000 currencies, timers, lootboxes, special draws, etc, etc. Basically a cauldron of shop-slop dumped over my screen in what I think was the hub/sanctuary/chill zone.

2/10, maybe even 1/10. It did nothing to engage me, just funnelled me through some linear, 2-second "fights" and then showed me everything I could spend real money on.

claims.claim: Unlocking characters without paying real money requires a heavy grind and long research times.

citations.review_text:
There are things that are great about the game. But it's growing to a very small list.
Pros: Cross progression between consoles. A somewhat satisfying gameplay loop (can be Improved) And a nice character roster, Pretty ladies, cool dudes. 
Cons: Said pretty ladies and cool dudes are a pain to unlock freely, and you can't unlock them all without spending real money.(that was a big thing I would have hoped fixed on my 2 year retreat) The research is still as bad as I remember. And The sudden spike in said gameplay loop forcing you to either Grind super hard or spend money. The last thing is the transaction difference between real money and their fake currency, it's not adjusted as I would have hoped, I get licensed content being a little more, but for the in game character skins not related to anything those should be a little cheaper, the devs really need to figure it out if they are also nerfing Descendants in a PVE game like the dumb devs from Helldivers 2 nerfing weapons in a PVE game, It makes no sense!

eh its ok for a free to play if you have some time on your hands. Things to shoot & stuff to level. Unsure exactly how long i'll stick with it as I'm getting a bit bored of the base 3 characters (yes 4 if we count bunny) but no way of getting a the others 'early' without paying or devoting a chunk of focus & grind time. (you need specific things you cant get at until you have completed XYZ & unlock NPCs/objective types)  Not sure I'm ready to sink real $ into it & I don't think I'll play it enough to get the suit I want. Basically the thing that would give me an incentive to play more & forget the time, is locked behind a pay/grind wall & at low levels that doesnt inspire me to sink even more time yet. Maybe if there was a quest at level X that gives you 1 'pick a non-ultimate character of your choice' instead of just Frenya.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe environments as empty, repetitive, and uninspired.

citations.review_text:
feels like a Warframe clone with an excessive focus on fan service. Pushing the game toward nudity and overly sexualized female character designs isn't going to create a better game or keep players interested in the long run.

I first played it at launch, and while it had potential and was at least somewhat enjoyable, I came back nearly two years later after all the updates and somehow it feels even worse. The gameplay is still clunky, the UI feels like it's designed for a mobile game, the environments are repetitive and uninspired, and the world feels empty and lifeless.

Instead of focusing on improving the gameplay, world, and story, it feels like the developers have leaned harder into aggressive monetization, pay-to-win mechanics, and fan service. Modern games seem too focused on selling cosmetics and appealing through sexualized designs instead of delivering memorable stories and polished gameplay.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a heavy and repetitive grind, particularly in the endgame or when farming materials and characters.

citations.review_text:
Honestly, The First Descendant is a masterclass in how to take a fun shooter framework and bury it under some of the most aggressive, soul crushing grind walls in recent memory. Running the same missions fifty times just to get a single piece of a character feels less like playing a video game and more like submitting to a part time job that doesn't pay. The boss fights are bullet sponges wrapped in cheap one shot mechanics, and the endgame loop gets stale faster than a loaf of bread left out on the counter.

With that being said, the developers clearly spent ninety percent of their budget and brainpower exclusively on the character design, and credit where credit is due, the gooner skins are absolute works of art. The physics engine is doing heavy lifting, the outfits are jaw droppingly unhinged, and you can tell the art team poured every ounce of their passion into making sure the characters look phenomenal while you are slowly losing your sanity. If you want a fun game, look elsewhere, but if you are just here to admire the digital tailoring and empty your wallet for maximum aesthetic culture, it delivers on that front.

I think I'm starting to finally understand the trend of these free to play games that I don't like. They are incredibly steeped in Microtransactions where you can pay for in-game things like the descendants, weapons, material etc or you can spend hundreds of hours grinding/farming the same repetitive, tediously boring, bland overland content for material and XP in order to not only have best in slot gear, but also get access to content that should not be blocked by any kind of grind, more specifically, Story content.

I gave The First Descendant a solid try, even coming back years after it's initial launch to see how far it's come but it wasn't enough, even after 36 hours, to keep me interested. As a Story-driven gamer, the story of First Descendant from what I have played (up to Season 2's story quest requiring you to be Master Rank 20, I was MR 12 to fight a Colossi) is very mediocre and super trope heavy and not all that entertaining especially not to grind for hundreds of hours to see if it gets any better. Weather it's seen as a clone of Destiny or just that Destiny and Warframe were heavy influncers, The First Descendant doesn't really feel like it does much to be unique or a stand out.

Pros:
-Visually it's pretty solid especially considering it's made in Unreal Engine 5
-Gunplay, while simple and easy to pick up it feels good.
-Voice acting for the characters that I came across were decent enough

Cons:
-Super grindy and repetitive gameplay loop with little to no diversity in activities and structure.
-Story is pretty forgettable and generic and leaves a lot to be desired espceially since exposition is through conversation briefings that feel very one side between missions and there are very few cutscenes throughout.
-Over Sexualization of Women all over the place and in your face. Skimpy and/or tight fitting outfits and incredibly unnecessary over the top "Jiggle physics" that thankfully can be turned down or off in the settings...if you go digg…
crazy ones you beat the story the game drops off the cliff, nothing to do but run same kill zones over and over

Reaching 100 hours now so it felt like a good time to spit out some pros and cons, to whoever is interested in a honest review:

1- I guess it's not rocket science to figure this point by yourself: Dont play this game if you dont like games with very, and i mean VERY sexualized characters. Not in a background/story sense, but more with the 1 million possibilities to costumize them being 999,999,999 cute & sexy options. Accept it.. Even youre not into it, most people around you will be wearing VERY revealing outfits. Is not something that will influentiate your gameplay at all, but your descendants will be ALL very attractive and beautiful and the means of costumize them with outfits and such, will always push more into the "Lets show as much skin possible" in a somehow reasonable and fun/cool looking way.

2- Grinding maybe will feel hard and frustrating sometimes, but trust me and others when we say: It was wayyyyyy harder back on start. Devs are doing a fairly good job imho, buffing this and that, increasing the chances of obtaining X or Y, and probably the most welcoming factor for newcomers being regular events where you can get a wide variety of vital things for free. And that leads me to the next and extremely important point in my eyes.

3- Micro transactions are 100% optional. Sure you can make a big list of games that work the same way, but this game does a pretty awesome job balancing the "Attracting players by offering free stuff vs Draining the wallets of the ones who stay and willingly want to buy things" - Dont get me wrong, i say this in a good sense. For exemple, if you enjoy the game, is fun progressing, unlocking new descendants etc. You grind hard and while at it, you think that would be cool to have another outfit/look on your descendant? Well, you can fairly easy get a free and tbf nice looking outfit. 

3.1- Between the multiple methods, i need to compliment the attendance events that been going non-stop, and the insertion of the attendace coin…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a repetitive mission structure and gameplay loop.

citations.review_text:
Definitely a 7.5/10!

First and foremost, its a free to play Looter Shooter. The game loops a small handful of objectives (Defend this circle, Kill all enemies, follow this drone, collect the orbs, etc). Sometimes the mission is a combination of them, especially around halfway through the main game. 

As far as the F2P and Microtransactions go, this game has a very good balance compared to others. The store is definitely there, but its perfectly viable to never look at it and have a great time. One of the 3 starter characters you can play as, Ajax, can singlehandedly clear the entire base game without doing anything other than hitting "Use recommended modules". Also completing the MSQ gave me Ultimate Bunny, which is one of the strongest characters in the whole game ($50 if you wanted to buy it for some reason)

The game absolutely loves to shower you in gear. Following the in game guide rewards you with a handful of legendary weapons that honestly feel broken because of how strong they are. A Machine Gun with infinite ammo, a Sword that can almost One shot all base game bosses, a Submachine Gun that can hit a dozen enemies with lightning, along with several others.

At the time of review I've spent 27 hours in game. In that time i got 5 characters to max level, completed the MSQ, unlocked 2 farmed characters, and got to Battle Pass (free tier) level 65. I had the game instant crash on 3 different play sessions, with no warning. There may also be a small memory leak, after extended playing there would be stutters, FPS drops completely randomly. 95% of the time the game ran locked at 75FPS with my build at 1080p and most settings maxed. 

The only complaints i have about this game really are the "fan service" aspects. The character outfits you can purchase teeter on grossly sexualized. The in game chat can get very yucky at times too.

Game was fun, but after doing the missions for a while they are just the exact same missions just in a different biome and terrain, they get really repetitive after a while. The cosmetics were cool and it was cool that you can get the paid cosmetics free just by grinding, when I seen that they had a Neon Genesis event going on I wanted to get them and I loaded in just to be told I can unlock the skins for free, then I looked into it more and you cant get a single character skin by playing and have to spend $100 just for them.

I think I'm starting to finally understand the trend of these free to play games that I don't like. They are incredibly steeped in Microtransactions where you can pay for in-game things like the descendants, weapons, material etc or you can spend hundreds of hours grinding/farming the same repetitive, tediously boring, bland overland content for material and XP in order to not only have best in slot gear, but also get access to content that should not be blocked by any kind of grind, more specifically, Story content.

I gave The First Descendant a solid try, even coming back years after it's initial launch to see how far it's come but it wasn't enough, even after 36 hours, to keep me interested. As a Story-driven gamer, the story of First Descendant from what I have played (up to Season 2's story quest requiring you to be Master Rank 20, I was MR 12 to fight a Colossi) is very mediocre and super trope heavy and not all that entertaining especially not to grind for hundreds of hours to see if it gets any better. Weather it's seen as a clone of Destiny or just that Destiny and Warframe were heavy influncers, The First Descendant doesn't really feel like it does much to be unique or a stand out.

Pros:
-Visually it's pretty solid especially considering it's made in Unreal Engine 5
-Gunplay, while simple and easy to pick up it feels good.
-Voice acting for the characters that I came across were decent enough

Cons:
-Super grindy and repetitive gameplay loop with little to no diversity in activities and structure.
-Story is pretty forgettable and generic and leaves a lot to be desired espceially since exposition is through conversation briefings that feel very one side between missions and there are very few cutscenes throughout.
-Over Sexualization of Women all over the place and in your face. Skimpy and/or tight fitting outfits and incredibly unnecessary over the top "Jiggle physics" that thankfully can be turned down or off in the settings...if you go digg…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the endgame content as lacking or falling off in quality.

citations.review_text: try it out it is free & fun. until you reach endgame that is lacking but not that bad.
Excessive waifu pandering but pretty on par if not better than Warframe's gameplay. MTX economy is iffy but more or less the same with other games of it's type. Endgame leaves a lot to be desired.

Honestly, The First Descendant is a masterclass in how to take a fun shooter framework and bury it under some of the most aggressive, soul crushing grind walls in recent memory. Running the same missions fifty times just to get a single piece of a character feels less like playing a video game and more like submitting to a part time job that doesn't pay. The boss fights are bullet sponges wrapped in cheap one shot mechanics, and the endgame loop gets stale faster than a loaf of bread left out on the counter.

With that being said, the developers clearly spent ninety percent of their budget and brainpower exclusively on the character design, and credit where credit is due, the gooner skins are absolute works of art. The physics engine is doing heavy lifting, the outfits are jaw droppingly unhinged, and you can tell the art team poured every ounce of their passion into making sure the characters look phenomenal while you are slowly losing your sanity. If you want a fun game, look elsewhere, but if you are just here to admire the digital tailoring and empty your wallet for maximum aesthetic culture, it delivers on that front.

claims.claim: Players describe the core mission design as repetitive, noting that objectives consistently follow the same formula of clearing enemies, reaching a point, and fighting a boss.

citations.review_text:
The game has very little content overall. If you're a new player, you might have fun with it for a week or so because everything still feels fresh, but the amount of time it takes to go from starting out to endgame is extremely short.

I honestly wouldn't recommend investing much time or money into this game. Here are a few things to consider:

1. The character balance is absolutely terrible.

The power gap between characters is way too big to just say "play whoever you like." In the endgame, some stages basically require specific characters and specific weapons to clear efficiently. There’s barely any room for strategy or alternative playstyles.

If you don't bring the "correct" character, you can even have random teammates leave the party. That's how bad the character balance is right now.

2. The content is repetitive and the mission design is extremely limited.

Pretty much every mission follows the same formula:

Kill enemies → go to a point → kill enemies → go to another point → kill the boss.

And that's basically it. The enemies are also constantly recycled, with only a few different types showing up over and over again. At most, the map looks a little different.

For a game that expects you to repeatedly grind for materials, this gets boring really fast. There’s just nothing particularly fun or interesting about doing the same thing over and over.

These two problems combined make the game feel even more empty. The terrible balance severely limits the number of characters that are actually worth playing, which makes you wonder what the point of releasing so many characters even is.

Then you have repetitive enemies and extremely limited mission types. Put everything together, and the game ends up feeling incredibly shallow and boring.

At this point, it feels like the game mostly has the character fanservice going for it.

And don't be fooled by the huge number of modules available in the game. In reality, you’re still using the same few builds over and ove…

Fun for a free to play game to a point though.

he then found out his account was linked to an old email address that no longer exists, contacted support to get it sorted out, and instead of helping, they closed his ticket without fixing anything. 3rd person sci-fi run-n-gun looter shooter.

It's addicting. Craft a crapton of guns and characters (descendants), and use them to kill a crapton of enemies. The descendants are all great, individual personalities, stories and combat styles. The scenery is gorgeous, the music is top-tier (every descendant has their own combat theme that plays while you're fighting during most missions), and the combat in general is super satisfying. And the storyline has been getting better and better every patch.

Cosmetics might be a mixed bag for most people. Store outfits are very expensive, but it's how the game keeps the lights on. Crossover events are only shop updates, But there is some amount of cosmetic rewards from all the events constantly going on, as well as the battlepasses, which are a bit better than the usual industry standard, so you will have outfits and skins to play with even as a free player.

The endgame is improving, bit by bit. Various missions types, and more being introduced every patch. You'll be happier if you enjoy collecting new weapons and descendants, and building them in various ways depending on the mission and enemy type. There is a playstyle for everyone, and the systems used to gather the blueprints and materials to make everything has been dramatically streamlined in recent patches, so nowadays it is more fun and less frustrating. And getting a new weapon or character is always exciting.

Speedrunning, farming, colossus fights, emoting in Albion, grinding achievements, changing your outfits and using the (admittedly slightly clunky and costly) dye systems, co-op, solo runs, testing builds in the laboratory, racing, training your doggo, decorating your private lounge and visiting others, and lots of other things to do in the game. There is actually a pretty huge amount of content for a new player.

Veteran players will bemoan the endgame, but these players have done everything in the game a hundred times over and are just waiting for …

The game gets fairly regular updates, that always include a new dungeon, character, or weapon. Also the Devs have made huge strives to simplify crafting systems. So while you have the grind of games like warframe you don't have all the unnecessary complexity of crafting that comes with those games.

Now the big elephant in the room, yes the paid skins are expensive. However, they give away a boatload of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and items by just logging in, watching on twitch, or completing simple tasks. If you cant afford the ridiculously priced skins, dont buy them, it detracts nothing from the actual game.

The gunplay is fun and so are the boss encounters, but I can't recommend this game because the devs don't respect the time of new players.

Two examples of what I'm referring to:

The Descendant Harris was once available from Eckert and his HQ missions. After doing some quick research, she hasn't been in the rotation list in a while. Yet the same items & Descendant's keep being rotated in-and-out. All through July and August it's the same rotation. No Harris. Same old stuff.

As a new player you have to grind for Harris and one required item drops at about 6 or 7 per dungeon run and you need 300 of them. I've been playing regularly for the last two months. If I hadn't logged in and played in the last 30 days I could unlock Harris by doing a stupidly easy task. 

So those that haven't been playing have Descendant's and items thrown at them, while new players have to grind.

The final irritation for me is the new event that allows you to buy past cleaning outfits with attendance mementos. As a new player I only have a few coins, which means that I will have to spend real money on caliber. Each outfit is 800 caliber. Again, those outfits were given out for free in the past so this seems to be only for long term players that have acquired these coins over time and not for new players. 

These outfits should be given out again for free to everyone. Give them to everyone and I'll change my review. Otherwise it stays to warn prospective players that the devs don't care about new players as much as they do the returning and OG players.
